body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-20 on 4ad3327f7, with a control.

    TMPDIR=/tmp/cwng-nospace-tmp      6817 passed, 112 skipped,  0 failed
    TMPDIR="/tmp/cwng space tmp"      6805 passed, 109 skipped, 15 FAILED

Same tree, same command, same 3-minute runtime. The only variable is the space.

## The 15

    tests/unit/test_set_ownership.py                  10
    tests/unit/test_dockerfile_calibre_symlinks_875.py 3
    tests/unit/test_947_non_root_container_starts.py   2

## Root cause — the PRODUCT IS FINE; the observation channels are not

`scripts/set_ownership.sh:172` quotes correctly:

    if "${CWA_CHOWN}" -R "${CWA_OWNER_USER}:${CWA_OWNER_USER}" "$dir"; then

The breakage is entirely in the harnesses, and it is the same mistake twice:

1. **`test_set_ownership.py` loses argument boundaries in its own recorder.** The
   stub is `echo "$@" >> "$CWA_TEST_CHOWN_LOG"` (line 47), which flattens every
   argument into one space-joined line, and `chowned_paths()` (line 137) then does
   `parts = line.split()` / `path = parts[-1]`. A path containing a space is
   therefore truncated to its last word. Measured:

       expected  /private/tmp/cwng space tmp/.../calibre-library
       recorded  tmp/.../calibre-library

   The assertion that fires — "library must be walked exactly once" — is reporting
   a defect in the recorder, not in the script under test.

2. **`test_947_non_root_container_starts.py` interpolates a path into a shell
   string unquoted**: `[str(HELPER), "/bin/sh", "-c", f"id -u > {marker}"]`
   (line 91). With a space in `marker`, the redirect target word-splits.

## Why this is worth a finding rather than a shrug

It cost two separate debugging cycles in one day — a delegate hit it and reported
15 failures, and the first attempt to reproduce it on a narrowed selection came back
CLEAN (176 passed, both with and without the space), because the `-k` filter did not
select any of the three affected files. **A negative from a narrowed probe is not a
negative**; only the full suite reproduces it.

It also invites the wrong conclusion. The natural reading of "chown walked the wrong
path when the path had a space" is a real container bug affecting anyone with a space
in a bind-mount path. It is not: the script quotes, the test does not.

## Fix shape (not attempted here — unrelated subsystem, and 15 tests across 3 files)

Record argument boundaries instead of flattening them: have the stub emit a
per-call marker plus one line per argument, and reconstruct in `chowned_paths()`.
Note `test_947` counts raw log lines (`calls == []`), so that consumer has to move
in the same change. And quote every path interpolated into a `sh -c` string.
title: Fifteen tests break when TMPDIR contains a space, because the test harnesses interpolate paths into shell contexts unquoted
